terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the passes here, and try your classes from main.

tasks.title: Make dates and times
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Dates` with two methods. `static LocalDateTime departure(String day, String time)` gives back the date and time that a day such as `"2031-03-04"` and a time such as `"14:05"` say; a text that is not one lets its exception reach the caller as it is. `static LocalDate onClipboard(int day, int month, int year)` gives back that date; a date that does not exist lets its exception reach the caller.

Check calls both with dates of its own, a 29 February among them, and with texts and dates that are not right. It reads a date as its text, and an exception by its type and whether its message names the text.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about making dates and times, and the errors they throw.
Write departure: read the day and the time each with its own type, then put them together.
Write onClipboard, and mind the order LocalDate.of takes its values in.
Try a date that does not exist from main, and read what is thrown.
hints: A date and a time of day are two types, and the type that holds both can be made from one of each. Each can read itself from text written the standard way.
Reading text that is not a date throws an exception that already names the text: departure needs no try at all. The method that makes a date from numbers takes the biggest part first.
`return LocalDateTime.of(LocalDate.parse(day), LocalTime.parse(time));` and `return LocalDate.of(year, month, day);`.

tasks.title: Count to a date
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Passes` with three methods. `static LocalDate expires(LocalDate bought, int months)` gives back the day a pass bought on `bought` for that many months runs out: the same day of the month, `months` later, or the last day of a shorter month. `static long daysLeft(LocalDate today, LocalDate expires)` gives back the days from `today` to `expires`, 0 on the day itself and below 0 once it has run out. `static long crossingMinutes(LocalDateTime leaves, LocalDateTime arrives)` gives back the minutes from `leaves` to `arrives`.

Check calls each method with dates of its own, years away from today, across the ends of months and years, and a crossing past midnight. `today` is always handed in: Check names the day.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about adding to a date, and about the gap between two.
Write expires, and try it from main on 31 January.
Write daysLeft for two dates months apart, then crossingMinutes.
Use the dates each method is handed, never the computer's clock.
hints: A month is not 30 days, and a gap of 1 month and 12 days is not 12 days. Java has a way to add each unit and to measure in each unit.

A date can add months to itself and keeps the day of the month when it can. A Period holds a gap in years, months and days, each apart; a unit such as days can measure the whole gap between two dates by itself. A Duration measures time with a time of day.
`return bought.plusMonths(months);`, `return ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(today, expires);` and `return Duration.between(leaves, arrives).toMinutes();`.

tasks.title: Print the day for the timetable
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `Timetable` with two methods. `static String heading(LocalDate day)` gives back the day as the timetable heads it, in English whatever the computer's language: the day of the week, the day of the month, the month's name and the year, as in `Tuesday 4 March 2031`. `static boolean runs(LocalDate day)` says whether boats run that day: every day but Sunday.

Check calls both with dates of its own, the last day of a year and a Saturday and a Sunday among them, and reads the heading letter by letter. It runs with the language of a computer in Germany, so a heading that follows the computer's language shows.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about formatting a date, and its table of pattern letters.
Write heading with a formatter that is told its language.
Write runs with the day of the week.
Try heading on 31 December 2029 from main, and look at the year.
hints: A pattern of letters says how a date is written, and the same letter means different things in small and capital letters. Names of days and months come from a language.

One letter four times gives the full name of a day; another, four times, the full name of a month. A formatter can be made with a pattern and a Locale. A date knows its day of the week as an enum value.
`DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("EEEE d MMMM uuuu", Locale.UK)`, then `return day.format(that);`, and `return day.getDayOfWeek() != DayOfWeek.SUNDAY;`.
